decisions.excerpt: Offer multiple ways to use your app or game. In addition to giving people the freedom to choose their

fields.title: Support accessibility in immersive experiences

statement.en: Ensure immersive apps and games support the accessibility features people use to personalize device interaction.
statement.ja: 没入型のアプリやゲームで、利用者が端末の操作方法を調整するためのアクセシビリティ機能に対応する。

conditions: Applies to the documented visionOS immersive experience; it does not invent a specific accessibility API or feature list.

decisions.note: Paragraph32 explicitly calls this essential. Separate the accessibility obligation from0005’s general recommendation to offer multiple ways to use the experience.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: As you design your models, keep the intended experience of your app in mind. It can take a long

fields.title: Align model design with the intended experience

statement.en: Design models with the intended app experience in mind and be ready to adapt data use and metrics when that experience changes.
statement.ja: 意図するアプリ体験を踏まえてモデルを設計し、その体験が変わる場合はデータの使い方や評価指標を調整できるようにする。

conditions: Model behavior can take time to change; plan adaptation rather than promising an immediate model redesign.

decisions.note: Paragraph4 adds experience-aligned model planning, distinct from0045’s input/output patterns. Role definitions and examples remain context for that existing planning rule.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: Request explicit feedback only when necessary. People must take action to provide explicit feedback, so it’s best to avoid

fields.title: Request explicit feedback only when necessary

statement.en: Request explicit feedback only when it is necessary, avoiding extra work for people where possible.
statement.ja: 明示的なフィードバックは必要な場合だけ求め、可能な限り利用者の追加作業を避ける。

conditions: Implicit feedback is a possible alternative, not permission or a requirement to collect more data.

decisions.note: Paragraph41 tempers only with best-to-avoid-if-possible; retain SHOULD, distinct from0001’s mandatory voluntary participation.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: Act immediately when you receive explicit feedback and persist the resulting changes. For example, if people identify content they

fields.title: Act promptly on explicit feedback

statement.en: Act immediately on explicit feedback and retain the changes it produces.
statement.ja: 明示的なフィードバックを直ちに反映し、その結果の変更を保持する。

conditions: Applies to received explicit feedback in general;0050/0051 separately address hiding unwanted content and preventing its return elsewhere.

decisions.note: Paragraph57’s general action/persistence outcome is broader than its unwanted-content example. One addition covers the general outcome without duplicating its two existing example-specific rules.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: In general, only use calibration when your feature can’t function without that initial information. If your feature can work

fields.title: Use calibration only when needed

statement.en: In general, use calibration only when the feature cannot function without the initial information it provides.
statement.ja: 通常は、初期情報がなければ機能が動作しない場合に限り、事前の調整・情報入力を求める。

conditions: If the feature can work without calibration,0055 separately permits other ways to gather the information.

decisions.note: Paragraph83 explicitly retains In-general; separate the recommended prerequisite from the existing MAY alternative rather than promoting either to MUST.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: Collect only the most essential information. Designing a unique experience that requests a minimal amount of information can make

fields.title: Minimize calibration information

statement.en: Collect only the information essential for calibration.
statement.ja: 事前の調整・情報入力では、本当に必要な情報だけを収集する。

conditions: Applies to information requested during calibration, not a direction to collect data for every feature.

decisions.note: Paragraph88 gives an unqualified only-most-essential privacy boundary. Apply the repository policy for privacy/data-minimization requirements;0035’s recommendation to infer remaining values is not the same collection limit.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: Continuously update your feature to reflect people’s evolving interests and preferences and help avoid mistakes. For example, you can

fields.title: Adapt to evolving interests

statement.en: Keep the feature updated as people’s interests and preferences evolve to help avoid mistakes.
statement.ja: 利用者の関心や好みの変化に合わせて機能を更新し、誤りを減らす。

conditions: Implicit feedback and relevant domain information are possible inputs to updates; ideally people need no extra work to benefit.
This does not itself authorize feedback collection or mandate a particular update interval.

decisions.note: Paragraph133 addresses ongoing adaptation, distinct from0010’s timing of feedback-driven updates.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: When possible, address mistakes without complicating the UI. Some patterns, such as corrections and limitations, tend to integrate seamlessly

fields.title: Avoid unnecessary mistake-handling complexity

statement.en: When possible, address mistakes without making the interface more complicated.
statement.ja: 可能な場合は、画面を複雑にせずに誤りへ対処する。

conditions: Balance a technique’s effect on the interface against the risk of worsening the original mistake, such as adding an incorrect explanation.

decisions.note: Paragraph135 preserves when-possible; none of the existing correction outcomes covers the interface-complexity tradeoff.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: List the most likely option first. When you know how your confidence values correlate with the quality of your

fields.title: Put the most likely option first

statement.en: Place the option most likely to meet the person’s goal first.
statement.ja: 利用者の目的に最も合う可能性が高い候補を、最初に提示する。

conditions: Use confidence for ranking only when its relationship to result quality is understood.
Context-based ranking and selecting the first option by default are possibilities when appropriate, not mandatory data collection or automatic selection.

decisions.note: Paragraph170 directs initial ordering;0070’s selection-feedback learning is related but not equivalent.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: In general, translate confidence values into concepts that people already understand. Simply displaying a confidence value doesn’t necessarily help

fields.title: Explain confidence with familiar concepts

statement.en: In general, express confidence using concepts people already understand.
statement.ja: 通常は、利用者がすでに理解している概念で信頼度を伝える。

conditions: A raw value may not explain its relevance to a result;0075 separately covers cases where people expect numerical or statistical information.

decisions.note: Paragraph181 states the general default; ranking, categories, and actionable suggestions remain narrower techniques, not complete substitutes.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

decisions.excerpt: Explain how limitations can cause unsatisfactory results. People can get frustrated when it seems that your feature works intermittently.

fields.title: Explain limitation-related poor results

statement.en: Explain how a feature’s limitations can lead to unsatisfactory results.
statement.ja: 機能の限界が、期待に届かない結果につながる理由を説明する。

conditions: Ideally the feature recognizes and describes the cause; this is not a guarantee of perfect diagnosis for every failure.

decisions.note: Paragraph231 states a result-specific explanation outcome. Merge the overlapping earlier list illustration rather than creating two rules; general expectation setting remains distinct.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

section_path: Getting your app to work with Siri

decisions.excerpt: To get the most out of Siri, an app can additionally associate its features and content with app schemas:

fields.title: Optionally associate content with app schemas

statement.en: An app may associate its features and content with app schemas to use the system’s existing domain understanding.
statement.ja: アプリの機能やコンテンツをApp Schemaに対応付け、システムが持つ分野ごとの理解を利用してもよい。

conditions: Applies to supported schema domains; examples such as email, music, and photos are not an exhaustive domain or availability list.

decisions.note: Paragraph6 says can additionally. This optional association is distinct from0017’s App Intents prerequisite.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

section_path: Getting your app to work with Siri

decisions.excerpt: An app can tell the system what’s onscreen by annotating its views and other content with app entities. This

fields.title: Optionally provide onscreen context

statement.en: An app may annotate onscreen views and content with app entities to give Siri contextual information.
statement.ja: 画面上のビューやコンテンツにApp Entityの情報を付け、Siriにその状況を伝えてもよい。

conditions: Annotations help interpret references to current app content; this rule does not authorize unrelated data sharing.

decisions.note: Paragraph9 explicitly describes an optional annotation mechanism absent from existing Siri rules.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

section_path: Getting your app to work with Siri

decisions.excerpt: To provide content information to the system, an app can donate entities to the on-device Spotlight index, which makes

fields.title: Optionally make entities searchable

statement.en: An app may donate entities to the on-device Spotlight index so people can find its content using Spotlight or Siri.
statement.ja: App Entityを端末内のSpotlightインデックスに提供し、SpotlightやSiriでコンテンツを見つけられるようにしてもよい。

conditions: 0002 separately guides which content is personally relevant; donation is optional and is not an instruction to index the entire catalog.

decisions.note: Paragraph10’s optional mechanism is distinct from content relevance and from action donation.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

section_path: Getting your app to work with Siri

decisions.excerpt: An app can also tell the system about actions a person takes while using it by donating the actions

fields.title: Optionally donate actions as intents

statement.en: An app may donate actions people take as intents so Siri can surface relevant future actions.
statement.ja: 利用者が行った操作をIntentとして提供し、Siriが今後に関連する操作を提示できるようにしてもよい。

conditions: Recent activity and items of interest are examples; do not infer a requirement to report every action.

decisions.note: Paragraph11 provides an independent optional action-context mechanism, not the mandatory App Intents integration outcome.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

section_path: Customizing your app’s experience with Siri

decisions.excerpt: For apps with many common feature sets, existing app schema domains provide the built-in functionality that they need to

fields.title: Optionally expose custom actions with App Shortcuts

statement.en: When functionality falls outside existing schema domains, an app may expose custom actions to Siri through App Shortcuts.
statement.ja: 機能が既存のSchemaの対象外である場合は、App Shortcutsを通じて独自の操作をSiriに公開してもよい。

conditions: This is a page-local integration option; it does not require every app to create custom shortcuts.

decisions.note: Paragraph24 says offer a way and preserves the outside-domain condition; no equivalent existing Siri rule.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

section_path: Customizing your app’s experience with Siri

decisions.excerpt: To customize the experience of an action or a piece of content associated with an existing schema, an app

fields.title: Optionally enrich schema responses

statement.en: An app may add optional intent or entity properties to enrich Siri responses for existing schemas.
statement.ja: 既存のSchemaでのSiriの応答を充実させるため、IntentやEntityに任意のプロパティを追加してもよい。

conditions: The system may omit optional properties in some contexts, including nonvisual ones.
A playback-control snippet is one example, not a required control;0006/0020 retain audible and self-contained voice response requirements.

decisions.note: Paragraph25 can-define and paragraph27 omission context support MAY; custom response-writing rules do not independently capture the option.
decisions.decision: add reviewed atomic rule; no existing rule replaced

coverage_resolution: Seventeen independently reviewed omissions across Immersive experiences, Machine learning and Siri. Conditions and overlap decisions are recorded per rule; all previously reviewed rules are preserved.
unverified: Source media, SDK availability, real payments, device behavior, App Review approval and external policies were not independently tested.

extraction_verification.method: Isolated extraction; all canonical rule files and stable-ID registry matched byte-for-byte.
